title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 2
statement: The weight of \(\frac{1}{3}\) of a large pizza together with \(3\frac{1}{2}\) cups of orange slices is the same as the weight of \(\frac{3}{4}\) of a large pizza together with \(\frac{1}{2}\) cup of orange slices. A cup of orange slices weighs \(\frac{1}{4}\) of a pound. What is the weight, in pounds, of a large pizza?

solutions.text: Let \(p\) be the pizza’s weight. A cup of orange slices is \(\frac14\) pound, so the two sides balance as \(\frac13 p + \frac72 \cdot \frac14 = \frac34 p + \frac12 \cdot \frac14,\) that is \(\frac13 p + \frac78 = \frac34 p + \frac18.\) Collect the pizza terms: \(\frac68 = \left(\frac34 - \frac13\right)p = \frac{5}{12}p.\) So \(p = \frac34 \cdot \frac{12}{5} = \frac95 = 1\frac45.\) Therefore, the answer is A.
hints: Let \(p\) be the pizza’s weight and convert cups of orange slices to pounds using \(\frac14\) pound per cup
Set \(\frac13 p + \frac72 \cdot \frac14 = \frac34 p + \frac12 \cdot \frac14\) and solve for \(p\)
